body:
EDGE TO WIRE BEFORE THIS IS PICKED UP: T120 (branch `t120-fifo`) is not in this store yet, so `ticket create` refused the edge — "edge to unknown ticket T120". Wire it with `adlc ticket update` once T120 lands. The contract: same file, same surface, review them together, and T120 is the more serious of the two because it hangs the door rather than misreporting to a CLI.

`loam user unlock` reports an empty answer as a clean one. A record file it could not READ, and a `--home` that is not a usable directory, both print "holds no login records / nothing to clear" and exit 0 — byte-identical to a healthy home where nobody has failed a login yet. In every one of those states the login door is charging NO name any delay, and this command is the only reader that looks at the file, so the fault is reported nowhere.

The likeliest instance is a mistyped `--home`. The most alarming is a symlinked `~/.loam` on an unmounted volume: the operator sees a tidy exit 0 while the limiter is entirely off.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN TICKET. It was built inside T116 and lifted back out. T116 records Myk's decision to replace the failed-login lock with a delay; its risk is timing and counting. This is filesystem taxonomy, and its correctness argument is a six-row errno table. Reviewed together, every reviewer paid for both — and the shapes were the thing nobody had considered, three rounds running. The limiter itself produced zero findings over the same span. Different surfaces, different reads, different PRs.

EDGE TO T120. Same file, same surface: T120 is the FIFO at `login-locks.json` that makes `readLocks` — and therefore the login door — block forever. Both are "what does this file do to us when it is not a healthy JSON file", and they should be reviewed together. T120 is the more serious of the two: it hangs the door rather than misreporting to a CLI.

EVIDENCE ALREADY PAID FOR — six review rounds inside T116 produced this, and it must not be re-derived. All of it was measured against the real module, not reasoned.

(1) THE HOME PREDICATE IS `statSync(home).isDirectory()` PLUS AN `X_OK` TRAVERSAL CHECK. Three wrong answers, each of which shipped and was caught:
  - `lstatSync(home)` alone SUCCEEDS on a dangling symlink, so a broken home stays silent. This is the bug the check was added to prevent, present in the first version of the check itself.
  - `lstatSync(home).isDirectory()` is the tempting one-token fix and CONDEMNS A HEALTHY symlinked home. Measured: lstat answers isDirectory=false for a working symlink to a directory.
  - `isDirectory()` alone says YES to a mode-0000 directory, because `stat` needs only a traversable PARENT. The home then passes and the record-file branch offers perishable-bytes advice for a file that can never exist there.
The discriminator table, measured:
    real       lstat: ok isDirectory=true    stat: ok isDirectory=true
    link       lstat: ok isDirectory=false   stat: ok isDirectory=true
    dangling   lstat: ok isDirectory=false   stat: THREW ENOENT
    file       lstat: ok isDirectory=false   stat: ok isDirectory=false
    missing    lstat: THREW ENOENT           stat: THREW ENOENT

(2) THE ACCESS MASK IS `X_OK`, NEVER `R_OK|W_OK|X_OK`. A read-only home is a SUPPORTED state — §36 criterion (o7), where a row stays frozen at its accumulated wait — and the wider mask condemns a home the door demonstrably reads. Measured:
    home mode   X_OK    R|W|X   door actually reads
    0000        DENY    DENY    0 rows
    0400 r--    DENY    DENY    0 rows
    0500 r-x    pass    DENY    1 ROW
    0700 rwx    pass    pass    1 row

(3) A BRANCH MAY NOT NAME A FAULT IT DID NOT DIAGNOSE. Two versions did, and both were measured against a sibling process churning the filesystem:
  - `lstat` merely SUCCEEDING was read as "it is a symlink". Against a sibling creating and removing a plain DIRECTORY, with no symlink anywhere: 32,587 of 887,391 calls — 3.7% — said "it is a symlink whose target is gone" and prescribed "repair or remove the link". The fix is `.isSymbolicLink()` on the stats object already held.
  - `accessSync` failing was read as "permissions", whatever the errno: 10,926 lines in 433,180 calls named ENOENT and then prescribed chmod.

(4) THE CURE MUST BE PER FAULT. One unconditional pair ("check --home, or run `loam init`") is right for a path that does not exist and misdirects everything else: an EACCES home was typed correctly and exists. Six faults, six cures: missing path; dangling link; not a directory; ELOOP; ENOTDIR (a non-directory path COMPONENT — reachable only through a FAILED stat, so it never reaches the isDirectory row); unreachable permissions.

(5) THE MESSAGE MUST NOT PREDICT A REPAIR. A read fault usually self-repairs — `readLocks` fails open and the next failed login writes a whole new table over the damage, DISCARDING the records nobody could read. But whether it happens turns on the door's policy (`maxTracked` below 1 writes no row at all) and on whether the path can be REPLACED, and the CLI knows neither. Measured across six read-fault states: five self-repair on one failed login, a DIRECTORY at the path does not — and its home is writable in every sense, so the discriminator is the path, not the home. So the message warns that the bytes are perishable and names no prediction.

(6) ONE BRANCH IS NOT REACHABLE FROM A TEST. The errno split inside the `accessSync` failure needs `access` to fail with something other than EACCES, which means the directory vanishing between the `stat` and the `access` — a race no fixture can force. Probed by collapsing that split: the rail stays GREEN. The branch must exist anyway, because the alternative prescribes chmod for a path that disappeared. Name the gap in the test file; a rail would need an injectable filesystem.

(7) A SHAPE-SHAPED RAIL IS HOLLOW BY CONSTRUCTION. Shapes are infinite and branches are not. Two branches (ELOOP, the fallback cure) were once deletable with the whole suite green. Rail the BRANCH LIST and probe each by deletion.

AND ONE LESSON ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT, because it nearly corrupted the evidence above: the first branch-deletion harness guarded on `git diff` to check its own patch had applied. The tree was legitimately dirty, so the diff was always non-empty and a pattern that never matched still printed a verdict — nearly reporting two sound branches as hollow and one hollow branch as sound. Guard a probe against a BACKUP COPY, never against git. An instrument that cannot fail is worse than a rail that cannot fail, because everything downstream inherits the wrong answer.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA belong in a working spec at `.adlc/specs/`, and (1) through (7) above are the rail list. The one behavioural promise to hold onto: an ABSENT record file on a usable home must still report an empty table and exit 0. That is the ordinary state of a home where nobody has failed a login, and a false alarm there is worse than the silence this ticket fixes.
title: `loam user unlock` reports an unreadable record file as an empty one — a tidy exit 0 over a limiter that is off
